thread.title: Apple Sinks on Fears of iPhone Weakness, Buy on the Dip?

author: investopedia.com
title: Apple Sinks on Fears of iPhone Weakness, Buy on the Dip?
text:
Apple Sinks on Fears of iPhone Weakness, Buy on the Dip? By Shoshanna Delventhal | November 13, 2018 — 12:54 PM EST
Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) and the companies in its robust ecosystem suffered share price losses on Monday following news that a Face ID recognition supplier reduced its outlook, citing a lowered shipment request from one of its biggest customers. With shares of the Cupertino, Calif.-based tech titan down nearly 18% from all-time highs reached in October, some see the recent weakness as a buy opportunity, while others are warning of more pain ahead for the high-flying FAANG player. Bears Concerned over Deteriorating End Demand for New iPhones
The lowered earnings forecast from Lumentum Holdings Inc. ( LITE ), a key Apple supplier, adds to speculation that the smartphone maker is reducing production of its latest iPhones in the key holiday season.
In a note on Monday, Wells Fargo gave Apple stock a market perform rating and wrote that "investors could consider Lumentum's updated guidance as reflecting as much as a 30% cut in Apple orders," as cited by CNBC . Bank of America analysts were more optimistic, writing that the announcement could indicate an inventory build and an earlier start to production, which "could magnify the perceived impact of these cuts." BofA added that new the iPad Pro also uses FaceID, so the announcement may not be directly translated to iPhone production.
While the tech behemoth has been hedging against slowing hardware unit sales with higher average selling prices (ASP) and a focus on its high growth Services business, the firm still generates nearly 60% of its total revenues from its iPhone business. Therefore, any indication of weaker iPhone sales could weigh on the company's financials, at least in the short term, as it transitions to a services-first business.
"We are concerned that end demand for new iPhone models is deteriorating," wrote Goldman Sachs analysts in a recent note, as cited by CNBC . "We note this could easily right itself given the bulk of demand comes in late December but we feel more prudent sell-through forecasts are warranted due to the timing and magnitude of this warning."
Goldman now expects Apple to produce 6% fewer iPhones in 2019 than previously expected, lowering its Apple stock price forecast from $222 to $209.
Shares of Apple are down 1.1% on Tuesday morning at $192.05, reflecting a 13.5% increase YTD, outperforming the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index's 5% rise and the S&P 500's 2.4% gain over the same period. Trading Center
